items.title: Ep29. How do earthquakes happen?
items.desc: In this episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Lily and Max head beneath the Earth’s surface to discover tectonic plates, faults, seismic waves and the enormous forces that can build up underground. With a simple hands-on experiment, they explore how rocks can get stuck, pressure can build, and a sudden slip can send vibrations travelling through the Earth.

items.title: Ep28. How big is the universe?
items.desc: In this episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Lily and Max zoom out from Earth to the Solar System, the Milky Way, and far beyond to discover just how enormous space really is.

items.title: Ep27. What is blood made of?
items.desc: After a tiny paper cut sparks a very dramatic “emergency,” Lily and Max take a closer look at the amazing stuff flowing through our bodies. Discover the four main parts of blood: plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets , and learn how they work together to carry oxygen, fight germs, deliver nutrients, and patch up cuts.

items.title: Ep26. How is tissue made?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max follow the journey from tiny wood fibres and watery pulp to giant drying machines, soft layers and neatly folded tissues in a box.

items.title: Ep25. How can chameleons change colours?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max discover that chameleons do not use magic, paint, or tiny artists. Instead, their skin has special colour cells and tiny crystal-like structures that reflect light in different ways. They learn that chameleons change colour to communicate, stay warm or cool, and sometimes help with hiding.
